chunks: Muhammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Mismaʿ al-Baṣrī, who said:
I prayed with Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, and he recited
"In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds."

Then he recited the surah that comes after al-Ḥamd, and he did not recite "Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm." Then he stood in the second rakʿah and recited al-Ḥamd, and he did not recite "Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm." Then he recited another surah.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This report does not contradict what we previously mentioned regarding the emphasis on reciting "Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm" aloud, because it contains the description of an action, and it is possible that Mismaʿ did not hear Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام reciting "Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm" due to a distance that was between him and the Imam. What clarifies what we have mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbd Allāh, Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the Imam being described in the report
key_terms.الثَّانِيَةِ: the second rakʿah of the prayer
key_terms.السُّورَةَ: the additional surah recited after al-Fātiḥah in salat
key_terms.الْجَهْرِ: audible recitation, specifically reciting aloud in prayer
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ: Sūrat al-Ḥamd, meaning Sūrat al-Fātiḥah in the prayer context
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: the transmitted report or hadith being interpreted
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ: the basmalah, whose recitation in prayer is under discussion

ai.seo_question: Does this hadith mean that بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ is not recited aloud in salat?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the observed prayer of Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام in which the narrator did not hear the basmalah before the later surahs. Al-Shaykh al-Ṭūsī explains that this does not negate the established emphasis on reciting the basmalah aloud, since the narrator may simply have been too far away to hear it. The report is therefore used in the discussion of salat recitation rulings.
